subject: general
question: Which two articles of the Constitution of India most clearly express the power of judicial review?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32 and Article 226**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 32 **of the Indian Constitution grants the **right to individuals to move the Supreme Court directly in case of any violation of their fundamental rights**.
 
• **Article 226 **provides the** power to High Courts to issue certain writs for the enforcement of Fundamental Rights** and for any other purpose.
 
• Judicial review refers to the power of the judiciary to review and determine the validity of a law or an order.
 
• Both Articles 32 and 226 play a crucial role in upholding the principle of judicial review in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Judicial Review**

 
 
• Judicial review is a process under which executive or legislative actions are subject to review by the judiciary.
 
• It is an essential function in a democracy as it ensures the supremacy of the Constitution.
 
 
 
• **Writs Issued Under Articles 32 and 226**
 
 
• Habeas Corpus: To ensure the release of a person unlawfully detained.
 
• Mandamus: To direct a public official or body to perform a public duty.
 
• Prohibition: To prevent a lower court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
 
• Certiorari: To transfer the matter from a lower court to a higher court for review.
 
• Quo Warranto: To challenge the legality of a person’s claim to a public office.
 
 
 
• **Fundamental Rights**
 
 
• These are a set of rights granted to the citizens of India, which are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution.
 
• They ensure civil liberties so that all Indians can lead their lives in peace and harmony as citizens of India.
 
 
 
• **Supreme Court of India**
 
 
• It is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court has extensive jurisdiction and is a guardian of the Constitution.
